source.title: Londonderry Sentinel, 22 January 1920, p. 3: "Derry Municipal Elections. South-East Electoral Area" (results table of all eleven counts, with the order of election, and an account of each count). Candidates' names as nominated: Londonderry Sentinel, 6 January 1920, p. 3 ("Londonderry Municipal Nominations of Candidates").
source.publisher: Londonderry Sentinel (via the British Newspaper Archive)
source.check: every count transcribed from the printed table and its account of each transfer; every count adds to the printed valid vote of 3,844, each result is the previous result plus the transfer, the quota is 3,844 / 13 + 1 = 296 as printed, the Unionist first preferences total 2,035 as the account says, and the order of election is the table's

note: Proportional representation (single transferable vote) under the Local Government (Ireland) Act 1919; polled 15 January 1920. Counted 20 January 1920 by Sir Henry Miller, returning officer. The area returned 12 members; Babington, Bonner and Bible became its aldermen. Seven Unionists and six Nationalists stood; the Unionists, 37 votes short of a seventh quota, lost the last seat (Mitchell). Magee (count 10) and M'Ananey (count 11) were elected last, M'Ananey on Gallagher's surplus. The table's non-transferable papers at counts 3, 4, 6, 8, 9 and 11 lay within the transferred quotas and are not shown as non-transferable votes. Party labels are the Sentinel's: its "N." covers the joint Nationalist, Sinn Féin and Labour ticket and does not say which of these each candidate stood for.
